course.title: Deep Reinforcement Learning
course.instructor: Chelsea Finn, with guest lecturers Archit Sharma, Aviral Kumar and Ashish Kumar

byLecture.2: Imitation Learning: transcript, slides, wiki page, 15 images

byLecture.4: Actor-Critic Methods: transcript, slides, wiki page, 21 images

byLecture.7: Offline RL: transcript, slides, wiki page, 14 images
byLecture.8: Reward Learning (conservative Q-learning, reward learning): transcript, slides, wiki page, 18 images
byLecture.9: RL for LLMs (guest lecture: instruction finetuning, RLHF, DPO): transcript, slides, wiki page, 24 images
byLecture.10: RL for LLM Reasoning (guest lecture: rejection finetuning, per-step credit assignment, per-step DPO, process advantage verifiers, thinking models): transcript, slides, wiki page, 27 images
byLecture.11: Model-Based RL (dynamics models, planning by backpropagation and sampling, CEM, model predictive control, the PDDM case study): transcript, slides, wiki page, 17 images
byLecture.12: Multi-Task RL (model-based policy optimization, when to use a model, multi-task imitation and RL, task identifiers, goal-conditioned RL, hindsight relabeling): transcript, slides, wiki page, 9 images
byLecture.13: Meta RL (the meta-RL problem, few-shot and in-context learning, black-box meta-RL, experience as a task identifier, meta-RL as a POMDP, off-policy meta-training, exploration and the coupling problem, posterior sampling): transcript, slides, wiki page, 19 images
byLecture.14: Exploration (regret, UCB and posterior sampling, the drug-trial bandit game, exploration in large MDPs from demonstrations and base models, learning to explore in meta-RL, DREAM and the variational information bottleneck, meta-exploration of student programs): transcript, slides, wiki page, 18 images
byLecture.15: Hierarchical RL and IL (long-horizon tasks, high-level and low-level policies, goal representations, supervising each level, when to move on to the next goal, hierarchical imitation with language and image subgoals, DAgger in language space, hierarchical RL, skill discovery): transcript, slides, wiki page, 20 images
byLecture.16: RL for Robots: Autonomous Learning (the reset problem, deployed and continuing policy evaluation, drift and state distribution collapse, forward-backward RL, MEDAL, the EARL benchmark, practising cycles of tasks, task proposals from a vision-language model, single-life RL): transcript, slides, wiki page, 25 images

byLecture.18: Frontiers (the last lecture: open problems in deep RL, from domains without rewards, prior data, video generation models as world models, value functions at scale and batch online RL to safety, calibration after RLHF, reliability and the evaluation of generalist systems; and how to do research: choosing problems, handling risk, getting things to work, pivoting, sharing work, mentorship and confidence): transcript, slides, wiki page, 15 images
byLecture.19: Tutorial Session: Review of Q-Learning (the TA session by Anikait Singh: Q-value iteration on a grid world, the optimal value, Q-value, policy and advantage, Monte Carlo, TD and n-step targets, stitching, semi-gradients and target networks, gradient clipping and the Huber loss, replay buffers, overestimation and critic ensembles; the DQN and soft actor-critic pseudocode from the slides only): transcript, slides, wiki page, 21 images

caveats: Lecture 1's recording leaves out the course-logistics slides (5-6 and 10-15); their content comes from the slides alone.
Lecture 2's recording ends after slide 21; slides 22-27 (collecting demonstrations, the embodiment gap, the summary) come from the slides alone.
Lecture 3's recording does not discuss slide 2's reminders and skips the KL constraint on slide 25 for time; that constraint comes from the slides alone.

Lecture 4's recording ends on the review slide (23); its slides 24-37 (off-policy actor-critic, replay buffers, soft actor-critic, the SAC-versus-PPO chart, the closing slides) are not discussed in that recording, but Lecture 5 teaches the same material aloud from a revised deck.

Lecture 5's recording covers slides 3-28; slide 2's reminders and slides 29-30 (plan recap, next time) come from the slides alone. Several steps (a KL-penalized objective, the clipping written out, the recursive Q-function) were worked on a board the recording does not show and are reconstructed from the spoken words.

Lecture 6's recording covers slides 3-29; slide 2's reminders and slide 29's next-week topics come from the slides alone. Slide 7's thought exercise is answered while pointing at the slide, and the algorithm is written on a board the recording does not show; the wiki reconstructs both from the spoken words and says so. Slides 24-25 print the n-step target's discount exponent as t - t', which the wiki notes as an apparent slip.

Lecture 7's recording covers slides 3-23 and 30-32. It does not teach the conservative-methods section (slides 24-28, conservative Q-learning) or slide 31's LinkedIn application, which Lecture 8 teaches aloud from the same slides, and it does not discuss slides 2 and 33. Much of the lecture is written or drawn live; the wiki reconstructs that work from the spoken words and says so. Slides 4, 18 and 19 print the Monte Carlo target's reward at t inside a sum over t', which the wiki notes as an apparent slip. In its worked advantage example the returns as captioned (+10, +1, -5) average to 2, not the 3 the lecturer uses; the wiki says so.

Lecture 8's recording covers slides 3-32; slides 2 and 34 (reminders, the guest-lecture announcement) and slide 33 come from the slides alone. Its CQL derivation and goal-classifier picture are worked on a board the recording does not show, the CQL objective in the critic's parameters rather than the slides' notation; the wiki reconstructs both from the spoken words and says so. In the recap's worked example the Q-value of the first action is written on the board and never read out. Slide 29 prints the RLHF stage's sub-line as the supervised stage's, which the wiki notes as an apparent copy slip.

Lecture 9 is a guest lecture by Archit Sharma from a deck based on CS224N slides; its 57 PDF pages print slide numbers 1-99 (hidden slides were not exported), and four unnumbered pages carry only the lowest label that fits. The recording follows the deck but does not discuss slides 81, 93, 97 and 98, which come from the slides alone. The cancellation of Z(x) in the DPO derivation is worked on a board the recording does not show; the wiki reconstructs it from the spoken words and slide 77. One pair of reward values in the Bradley-Terry scale example is garbled in the captions.

Lecture 10 is a guest lecture by Aviral Kumar. Its recording covers slides 2-27 and then slide 32; slides 28-31 and 33-41 (thinking models: the formulation, meta strategies, response length, test-time scaling, leaderboards, open questions) come from the slides alone. Its rejection finetuning algorithm, language MDP and per-step DPO algorithm are written on a board the recording does not show; the wiki reconstructs them from the spoken words and says so. Its result charts on slides 10, 19 and 23 are only the first frame of an animation, so those results come from what the lecturer says.

Lecture 11's recording covers slides 4-25 and 32-36. Finn leaves model-based policy optimization for the next lecture, so slides 26-30 (its augmented roll-outs and full algorithm, when to use model-based RL, other kinds of models) and the reminders (2, 37-38) come from the slides alone; Lecture 12 teaches that material aloud from its own version of those slides. The gradient-based planning algorithm, a latent-state model and the optimization sketches are worked on a board the recording does not show; the wiki reconstructs them from the spoken words and says so, including a sign the lecturer corrects aloud. Slide 34's charts are partly covered by a text box on the slide.

Lecture 12's recording covers slides 3-25 and the start of slide 26, and ends at about 1:10:21: the rest of slide 26 (relabeling with the last state as goal), slide 27's HER results and slides 28-29, and slide 2's reminders, come from the slides alone. The model-based policy optimization algorithm, the combined MDP's reward and dynamics, the multi-task imitation objective and the relabeling algorithm are written on a board the recording does not show; the wiki reconstructs them from the spoken words and says so. Slide 24 prints 'task 2 ID' where Finn says task 1 (passing) is meant, and slide 18's sum over tasks runs to T where Finn speaks of n tasks. Its transcript has 6 [Ed:] notes.

Lecture 13's recording covers slides 3-37; slide 2's reminders and slides 38-39 (plan, next time, reminders) come from the slides alone. The black-box meta-RL algorithm, its meta-test steps and a discount factor are written on a board the recording does not show; the wiki reconstructs the objective from the spoken words and says so. Slide 20 holds frames of two maze videos whose content comes from what Finn says. Slide 22 prints the venue of Qu et al.'s test-time compute paper as ICML 2019. Its transcript has 4 [Ed:] notes, among them a garbled word after PPO and a restored 'decouple'.

Lecture 14's recording covers slides 3-32; slide 2's reminders and slides 33-34 (plan, reminders) come from the slides alone. Slide 12 prints only 'Exploration game': the drug-trial bandit game runs on a website the PDF does not contain, so the wiki describes it from the transcript. Finn's regret curves and the bottleneck, objective and exploration-reward derivations are drawn where the recording does not show them; the wiki reconstructs them from the spoken words and the slides. Slides 21-23 print the KL penalty's unit Gaussian as N(0, 1); Finn corrects it to the identity, and the wiki writes N(0, I). Slides 27, 30 and 31 hold video frames. Its transcript has 4 [Ed:] notes, among them a garbled phrase in the drug game and the reward's arguments at about 1:02:05.

Lecture 15's recording covers slides 3-44 and closes on slide 46's 'next time'; slide 45's summary outline and the reminders on slides 2 and 46 come from the slides alone. Finn draws the hierarchical policy, the roll-out procedure, a pasta-making example's sets of states (which no slide holds), a demonstration's segments and an image-subgoal policy on a board the recording does not show; the wiki describes them from the transcript. Slides 23, 31-33, 35, 36 and 39 hold video frames or stills, whose content comes from the transcript, and slide 43's video is a black square in the PDF. Slide 34's left-hand chart prints no axis values, only its 19% and 34% gaps.

Lecture 16's recording covers slides 3-45 and ends on slide 45's summary; the reminders and 'next time' on slides 2 and 46 come from the slides alone. Its deck prints a slide number on only three pages (28, 30, 32), each equal to its page, so every label is the page number. Finn writes the reset-free experience, the evaluation formulas and the forward-backward and task-cycle algorithms on the slides where the recording does not show it; the wiki describes them from the transcript and the slides that follow. Slides 8, 26, 30, 31, 33, 39 and 42-44 hold video frames whose content comes from the transcript. Slide 13's continuing-evaluation sum starts at t = 0 where Finn says t = 1.

Lecture 17 is a guest lecture by Ashish Kumar; its recording (about 50 minutes) covers slides 2-78 and ends on slide 78's question, and slide 79 and slide 1 are not discussed. Seven student questions, inaudible and mostly restated by Kumar, come between slides 41 and 42. Its deck prints a slide number only on 62-67, each equal to its page, so every label is the page number. Most of its pictures are frames of videos (slides 5-11, 22-27, 30, 31, 33-36, 45, 58, 62, 67, 69, 70, 73, 74, most likely 55-56), whose content comes from the transcript; slide 46 is blank in the PDF. Slide 16's reward terms are printed without definitions of their symbols, and the captions are unclear where Kumar names the first terms.

Lecture 18 is the course's last lecture, given by Chelsea Finn (the deck prints no lecturer name); its recording (about 71 minutes) opens on the plan for both parts and ends on slide 52's closing thoughts. Slide 2's reminders are not mentioned and slide 53's thank-you is not read aloud, so both come from the slides alone. Its deck prints no number on slides 40, 52 and 53, but every label is the page number. Five student questions, inaudible and restated by Finn, are answered in place; the one at about 32:29 is restated only as 'why does this happen', and the wiki reads it as being about the loss of calibration after RLHF from the answer. Several slides are tied to examples whose videos or demos are not in the PDF (slides 8, 12 and 39).

Lecture 19 is the Q-learning TA session, given by Anikait Singh; its recording (about 51 minutes) ends on slide 31 during the discussion of critic ensembles, so slides 32-35 (the walkthrough of the Homework 2 algorithms, with DQN and soft actor-critic pseudocode) come from the slides alone. Its deck prints a number only on the title page, so every label is the page number. The Monte Carlo, TD and n-step derivation and the TD loss are worked on a whiteboard the recording does not show; slide 20 prints the derivation's lines, and the wiki reconstructs the loss from the spoken words and says so. Unlike the other recordings, three student questions are captioned and kept in quotation marks; five more are inaudible. Its transcript has four [Ed:] notes.

Lectures 1 and 2 each have three passages marked [Ed: unclear], Lecture 3 one, Lecture 4 two, Lecture 5 five (plus four flagged restorations). Lecture 6's captions are much noisier: 53 of its 80 paragraphs carry [Ed:] notes, mostly on garbled board dictation and mis-heard notation. Lecture 7's captions are cleaner: 8 [Ed:] notes in 7 of its 88 paragraphs. Lecture 8 has 4 [Ed:] notes in its 86 paragraphs, Lecture 9 6 in its 81, Lecture 10 7 in 5 of its 92 (among them a garbled sampling temperature and two garbled benchmark or model names), and Lecture 11 6 in 6 of its 95 (among them a horizon captioned as a number and a reward function captioned as letters), Lecture 12 6 in its 92, Lecture 13 4 in its 90, Lecture 14 4 in 3 of its 94, Lecture 15 none in its 91, Lecture 16 none in its 85, Lecture 17 4 in 3 of its 65 (a word that may be world or board, two garbled phrases about the reward function and simulator, and one about the size of the extrinsics), and Lecture 18 2 in its 92 (a word that may be competent or confident, and a phrase where slide 43 prints 'Start from something that works').
